title: 3.7.4 Lab: Transform a List Without Mutating the Input
description: Use .map() to build a transformed copy of an array, then demonstrate the original is unchanged. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the source list
steps.instructions: The starter gives you an array of numbers (the lesson calls it prices; you may rename it): const prices = [10, 20, 30]; Leave its three numbers as they are.

steps.title: Build a transformed copy with .map()
steps.instructions: Use .map() on prices to build a new array where each number is transformed (for example, doubled), and store the result in a second variable (the lesson calls it doubled; use any name that fits).

steps.title: Log both arrays
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print the transformed array and the original prices array. Confirm the original still holds its starting values.

requirements.title: Array declared
requirements.description: Declares an array with square brackets. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Keep the array the starter gives you (the lesson calls it prices). Its values stay as they are.

requirements.title: .map() used
requirements.description: Calls .map() to build a transformed array. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Call .map on prices with a function that changes each number, and keep the result in a second variable.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Print the new array and then prices, so you can see the original did not change.

requirements.title: prices still holds its starting values and both arrays are printed
requirements.description: prices is still [10, 20, 30], doubled holds three transformed numbers, and the output shows them. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: .map() builds a new array and leaves prices alone. Store the result in a second variable and do not assign into prices.

checks.expr: Array.isArray(doubled) && doubled.length === 3 && doubled.some((x, i) => x !== prices[i]) && (J => doubled.every(x => J.includes(String(x))))(output.join(' ')) && !same('doubled', 'prices')
checks.fail: doubled should hold the three transformed numbers, and your output should show them (and the original prices).

requirements.title: doubled is built from prices and printed by code that runs
requirements.description: When prices holds other numbers, doubled changes with it, and a console.log that runs prints doubled. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Build doubled with prices.map(...) and print doubled itself. A list typed in by hand, or typed-in output, does not change when prices does.

checks.fail: doubled has to be computed from prices with .map(): when the checker changes the numbers in prices, doubled must change with them. A list typed in by hand stays the same.
Print doubled with console.log, by code that runs: the printed numbers must be the ones .map() made. Typed-in numbers do not count.
